traps.why: An alkoxide with a 2°/3° halide does E2, not SN2: you get the alkene, never this ether. To make the ether, put the hindered group on the alkoxide and use a CH₃/1° halide.

explanation: Methoxide/ethoxide is a strong base; with a 2° or 3° halide it removes a β-hydrogen (E2) to give the Zaitsev alkene. No ether forms.
